Recode categories by name

Source: R/catg.R
grdrcd.Rd

grdrcd() recodes a categorical column by an explicit mapping from old to new labels and refuses any observed value the mapping does not name: silent pass-through is how group labels get corrupted. deccodes() decodes numeric category codes with a code-to-label dictionary (codes as names), the step that turns the codes of an imported file into its categories. relbl() relabels a variable by name, never by position, and returns a factor whose levels follow the mapping.

Usage

grdrcd(x, map, keep = character())

deccodes(x, vlabs, keepna = TRUE)

relbl(x, map, keep = character())

Arguments

x

The labels or codes: a vector or a factor.

map, vlabs

A named character vector: old label (or code) = new label.

keep

Values that pass through unchanged.

keepna

FALSE refuses missing codes.

Value

grdrcd() and deccodes(): a character vector the length of x. relbl(): a factor.

Details

Assigning labels by position is how category codes get rotated: when the labels are listed in alphabetical order and the codes are not, every group receives its neighbour's label. Mapping by name makes the assignment independent of any order.

In grdrcd() a value listed in keep passes through unchanged and missing values stay missing. In relbl() every level (the levels of a factor, or the sorted distinct values) must be mapped or kept; the levels of the result are the new labels in the order of the mapping, then the kept values that occur. The result carries an attribute recode: the mapping and the kept values.

See also

grdlvls(), declbld(), vrfrcd(), vrfmrg().

Examples

# simulated race codes of an imported file
codes <- c(1, 2, 2, 3, 1, NA)
deccodes(codes, c("1" = "White", "2" = "Black", "3" = "Indigenous"))
#> [1] "White"      "Black"      "Black"      "Indigenous" "White"     
#> [6] NA          
#> attr(,"recode")
#> attr(,"recode")$mapping
#>            1            2            3 
#>      "White"      "Black" "Indigenous" 
#> 
#> attr(,"recode")$kept
#> character(0)
#> 
grdrcd(c("M", "F", "F", "X"), c(M = "Male", F = "Female"), keep = "X")
#> [1] "Male"   "Female" "Female" "X"     
#> attr(,"recode")
#> attr(,"recode")$mapping
#>        M        F 
#>   "Male" "Female" 
#> 
#> attr(,"recode")$kept
#> [1] "X"
#> 
relbl(factor(c("a", "b", "a")), c(a = "Adult", b = "Youth"))
#> [1] Adult Youth Adult
#> attr(,"recode")
#> attr(,"recode")$mapping
#>     a     b 
#> Adult Youth 
#> 
#> attr(,"recode")$kept
#> character(0)
#> 
#> Levels: Adult Youth
try(grdrcd(c("M", "F", "U"), c(M = "Male", F = "Female")))
#> Error : grdrcd: values with no mapping: 'U'. Every observed category must be mapped by name (or listed in `keep`).
